html:
The Havasupai, or Havasu Baaja, are a Native American people who live in Havasu Canyon, a side canyon of the Grand Canyon in northern Arizona. Their name means "people of the blue green water", after the creek and waterfalls of their canyon.

They speak an Upland Yuman language close to that of their neighbours the Hualapai. For centuries they farmed maize, beans and squash on the canyon floor in summer and hunted and gathered on the plateau above in winter.

In the 1880s the United States confined them to a small reservation on the canyon floor, cutting them off from their winter lands. In 1975 Congress returned a large part of the plateau to them. Their village, Supai, can still be reached only on foot, by mule or by helicopter. See also the Havasupai page and the neighbouring Yavapai.
